column2: The sandbenders do not move the desert so much as persuade it. Their forms are earthbending, and nothing at all like the earthbending you were taught.
Ask them to teach you their way
Study what you can for now
Years on, the trick of it finally clicks. The grain beneath the grain, and how little force it takes once you stop fighting the desert.
Every element keeps a secret inside it, and earth hides hers deepest. Stone, sand, iron, and the molten heart far below. Whichever of them opens, it will not open twice.
Listen for the iron in the stone
Loosen your grip on the sand
Feel the world through your feet
Fire is a simple thing. It burns. But simple things have more than one shape, and fire has several, each of them dangerous, and each of them waiting.
Split the flame cold and clean
Gather it to a single point
Water is the element of change, and it changes in ways the tribes mention only in whispers: the hand that mends, and the hand that takes hold of the water inside a living body.
Learn to mend what is broken
Air is not emptiness. Past the gliding and the gusting there is a place where the body finally forgets to be heavy, and past that, a place where it forgets to be at all.
Ask the sandbenders to teach you
Ask to be taught the healing arts

At the North, the healers keep to their own hall, and the warriors keep to theirs. The teacher says you may look, if you like. The art of mending is old here, older than the war, and it is not taught to every visitor.
Ask the healers to take you on
Your path lies with the warriors
The healers work in silence, drawing water to the wound and willing it to remember what whole flesh is like. It is slow, delicate work, and nothing like bending in anger.
